Presence/absence test between conditions (Fisher exact)

Source: R/quant-stats.R
test_detection.Rd

Complements test_differential() for the features a quantitative test cannot rank: those detected in one condition and (nearly) absent from the other, which in immunopeptidomics are often the biologically interesting ligands. For every feature and contrast a Fisher exact test is run on the 2x2 table of detected / not-detected units, with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment within the contrast. Their fold change is undefined by construction — imputing one would make it an artefact of the imputation width — so detection frequency, not intensity, is what is tested.

Usage

test_detection(mat, coldata, contrasts = NULL)

Arguments

mat

Numeric matrix (before or after imputation; detection is taken from the imputed attribute when present, otherwise from !is.na(mat)).

coldata

Column metadata from build_quant_matrix().

contrasts

List of length-2 character vectors, or NULL (default) for all pairwise comparisons.

Value

A data frame with Contrast, Feature, n_det_ref, n_tot_ref, n_det_test, n_tot_test, P.Value_det, adj.P.Val_det and Exclusive_in (the condition name when the feature is detected in one condition only, NA otherwise).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
det <- test_detection(qm$mat, qm$coldata)
subset(det, !is.na(Exclusive_in) & adj.P.Val_det < 0.05)
} # }
